note: PROPOSED SHAPE ONLY -- no production /review endpoint change has been made. These vectors show what the review-domain profile's records WOULD look like once the admission leg (request_capture_ref/admission_index/accepted_at/response_deadline + the admission-as-gate/two-dimensional-obligation shape from PR #5 commit 3508e49) is actually implemented. Disposition side (verdict_published/failed_with_reason) already matches our live decision_ref preimage (verdict/artifact_hash/policy_version/source_class/vantage_limitation) today -- admission side does not exist in production yet.
response_deadline_derivation: PROPOSED: response_deadline = admitted_at + POLICY_SLA_SECONDS[policy_version], POLICY_SLA_SECONDS['invinoveritas.review.v5'] = 60. Grep-verified 2026-08-02: no timeout/SLA constant for /review exists in core/models.py or app.py today -- this is a genuinely new number, not a documented-but-unwired one. 60s is generous relative to typical sub-10s LLM-backed review latency; open to revision once a real production value is committed.

reachable: pending|open (theoretically, between accept-commit and verdict-commit within one HTTP call; unobservable today -- no GET /review/{admission_index} query endpoint exists to catch it mid-flight)
unreachable_by_construction: cancelled -- no requester-withdrawal path exists on /review today; would need a real async mode or a pre-verdict cancel endpoint, neither built
reachable_subset.why_liveness_failure_is_reachable_at_all: Per Merlini's second fork (2026-08-02, trustless-ai group): even though the HTTP transport stays synchronous, an admission_receipt would be committed at the commitment layer BEFORE the verdict-commit, microseconds apart within the same call. A crash/dropped-connection/quiet-decline between those two commits (e.g. the LLM call itself throwing) is exactly the failure our own /ledger raw-tape-vs-published gap (219 vs 214, completeness block) already discloses statistically -- this profile makes it a per-request falsifiable predicate instead.

cases._annotation: the normal path: a real /review call, artifact admitted, verdict lands well inside the SLA. verdict_published as a disposition KIND covers all 3 of our real verdict values (approve/approve_with_concerns/reject) -- the obligation is 'did we produce a verdict', not which one; the semantic verdict value lives inside the disposition payload, outside this core's concern.

dispositions._verdict_value_note: e.g. approve_with_concerns -- not read by the core, informational only

cases._annotation: real today: an invalid artifact_type currently 422s with no persisted record at all. Under this profile it becomes a gate outcome (per Pavlo's fix, 2026-08-02 group thread) -- a rejection receipt referencing the request_capture, but no obligation is ever created. Matches the core's own generic P1 case shape.

real gap today: a genuine processing failure (LLM call errors, provider timeout) either 500s unrecorded or silently retries -- indistinguishable from a reject verdict, which means 'reviewed and found unsound', not 'couldn't review'. failed_with_reason is the honest terminal for this.

THE motivating case: accept-commit lands, then the process crashes/drops before verdict-commit (as_of evaluated past the deadline, no disposition yet exists). This is the per-request predicate that replaces our /ledger's statistical raw-tape-count check -- 'accepted and then silently produced nothing' now resolves to a provable liveness_failure instead of indistinguishable-from-never-asked.

ASOF pair, part 1/2 (Pavlo's explicit-as_of gate, applied to this profile). Same admission_index as the pair below, evaluated BEFORE a late verdict is committed -- an honest auditor querying right after the deadline sees liveness_failure.

ASOF pair, part 2/2. SAME admission (10045) as the case above, but evaluated AFTER a retried verdict eventually lands, well past the deadline. The two facts are independently recomputable and neither erases the other -- 'unresolved|liveness_failure' was true at as_of=4070 and stays true there forever; 'resolved:verdict_published|late' is what a later observer sees. Exactly Merlini's NC5 discipline (2026-08-02: 'a late verdict is resolved:verdict_published|late -- resolved AND the breach preserved, both recomputable'), applied to a real /review retry scenario.

real design consideration, not yet solved: /review has no idempotency key visible at the admission layer today. A client-side retry after a slow/ambiguous response could plausibly cause two independent verdict-commits against the same admission_index. This profile surfaces that as conflict rather than a silent overwrite -- but building the actual idempotency-key mechanism to PREVENT it is separate, real, un-scoped work, flagged honestly here rather than assumed solved by naming the terminal.

defensive case: the admission's captured_object_hash doesn't match the capture's own object_hash -- e.g. the artifact was mutated between capture and admission. Core-level binding check, no review-specific logic needed.
